connector: Close your eyes and picture a busy market: people shouting, animals in the street, bread in the oven. Today’s article takes you to a medieval town. Look for what made it so loud, so busy, and so smelly.

a.raw: in the town of york merchants sold wool every week
a.fixed: In the town of York, merchants sold wool every week.
a.why: In starts the sentence. York is the name of a place. A comma comes after the opening part, In the town of York. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: in old london bakers sold bread near the river thames
b.fixed: In old London, bakers sold bread near the River Thames.
b.why: In starts the sentence. London is a place. A comma comes after the opening part. River Thames is the name of one river, so both words get capitals. A period ends the sentence.

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Barber-Surgeon
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A barber in a medieval town did more than cut hair and shave beards.
Barbers also pulled bad teeth and treated cuts and wounds.
Stories say the red and white stripes on a barber pole are a reminder of that old job.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Can you smell that? Today we visit a medieval town. It was loud, busy, and often smelly. Let’s find out why.
transcripts.guide1: Word study. Build script and scribe words, name what details are about, and break words apart.
transcripts.guide2: Read about medieval towns. Look for what you could see, hear and smell.
transcripts.guide3: Today you check your paragraph for capitals and periods.

notes.wordParts: The root script or scribe means write. describe = to write about something. manuscript = written by hand. One root, two spellings.
notes.grammar: A paragraph has one main idea, often in the first sentence (the topic sentence). The other sentences are details that support it. A sentence that does not support it is off the topic.
notes.spelling: -ful means full of (hopeful). -less means without (hopeless). -ness turns a describing word into a thing (kindness). -ly tells how something was done (quickly).
notes.wgrd: Details you can see, hear and smell help you picture a place. Ask what caused each one.
vocab: a group of craftsmen or merchants in the same trade
a person who buys and sells goods for profit
the buying and selling of goods

plate.alt: An old wall painting of a town street: people dancing to a tambourine on the left, and shopkeepers at an open shop with a man and a donkey on the right
plate.credit: Effects of Good Government in the City (detail) · Ambrogio Lorenzetti, 1338–1339 · Palazzo Pubblico, Siena · Public domain
plate.look: Part of a huge wall painting in the town hall of Siena, Italy, painted almost 700 years ago. On the right, shopkeepers work at an open shop, and a man stands with a donkey. A rider passes by up above. On the left, people dance in the street to a tambourine. A medieval town was busy and full of life.
